duoNoel.setupTitreDuo: Which Christmas characters are you two?
duoNoel.setupDescDuo: Enter your first names. The first one answers the twelve questions about your Christmas together, passes the phone, and the second one takes their turn. At the end you'll see the Christmas duo you make, the one each of you would have got on your own, and the questions where you don't agree.
duoNoel.setupTitreSolo: Which Christmas characters are you two?
duoNoel.setupDescSolo: Twelve questions about your Christmas together: the tree, the presents, the dinner, Christmas morning... Answer with the two of you in mind, and find out which Christmas duo you make.
duoNoel.chacunMeme: On your own, you would both have got the same duo. You do Christmas the same way!
duoNoel.chacunGagne: Your duo is {{nom}}'s: {{autre}} gave it good marks too.
duoNoel.chacunCompromis: Neither of your two duos wins: the couple's duo is the compromise, the one that's like you both.
duoNoel.chacunContraste: {{nom}} answered like Scrooge, {{autre}} like someone who loves Christmas: that's exactly this duo.
duoNoel.accordHaut: You see Christmas in more or less the same way.

duoNoel.p_noel_d: At your place, Christmas is planned like a delivery round. The lists are written in November, the presents are wrapped before anyone else's, and the family usually ends up at your house. You think of everyone, even the cousin who always gets forgotten. Your favorite present is the look on people's faces when they open theirs.
duoNoel.p_noel_a: By looking after everyone else, you end up last on your own list. Keep one evening just for the two of you, with a present you won't open in front of anyone.
duoNoel.p_lutins_d: You can't do Christmas without using your hands. Homemade presents, parcels wrapped far too well, hand-drawn cards, reindeer-shaped cookies... and a prank or two on top. You've stayed big kids, and December is the month when you're finally allowed to show it.
duoNoel.p_lutins_a: Start earlier this year. A handmade present at midnight on the 23rd gets glue everywhere and ends in an elf quarrel!
duoNoel.p_epices_d: For you, Christmas is something you eat. You've been thinking about it since the fall: the menu, the cookies, the market for the good ingredients, the dessert you make twice because the first one wasn't pretty enough. The kitchen is where you spend the holidays, and it's where you're happiest.
duoNoel.p_epices_a: Cook together, but decide beforehand who's in charge: there's only room for one chef at the oven. And keep some cookies for yourselves.
duoNoel.p_tomtes_d: Your Christmas happens in the living room. A blanket, candles, thick socks, a cheese fondue, a movie you know by heart. You don't need a crowd and you don't need to go out: like the little Scandinavian gnomes who watch over the house, you're perfectly happy at home, just the two of you.
duoNoel.p_tomtes_a: Say no to every other invitation, without feeling guilty. And treat yourselves to the best blanket in the store: you're going to wear it out.
duoNoel.p_neige_d: Your Christmas happens outdoors, or at least not far from a window. A walk in the cold, a real tree that smells of the forest, a good sweater, and you're happy. You don't need ten strings of lights or three Christmas dinners: a little snow is enough, as long as the other one is there.
duoNoel.p_neige_a: If it doesn't snow this year, go and find the snow: a weekend in the mountains beats any present. And remember the thermos.
duoNoel.p_noisette_t: The Nutcracker and the Sugar Plum Fairy
duoNoel.p_noisette_d: You're the most magical couple of December. The lights, the shop windows, the Christmas market, a show or an old Christmas movie: you want everything to sparkle. At your place the table is beautiful, the tree is color-coordinated, and you dress up for Christmas Eve even when it's just the two of you.
duoNoel.p_noisette_a: Give each other an outing rather than an object: a ballet, a concert, an ice rink at night. That's the kind of memory you keep.
duoNoel.p_rennes_d: At Christmas, you're mostly on the road. One dinner here, one lunch there, a suitcase that never gets unpacked and a trunk full of presents. You're the couple everyone is waiting for, and you always make it, even two hours late and with one parcel left behind.
duoNoel.p_rennes_a: Pulling the sleigh is tiring. Block out one day with no car and no invitations over the holidays: the couch has its charm too.
duoNoel.p_scrooge_d: At your place, one of you rolls their eyes at the first Christmas song, and the other has already got the decorations out. Or maybe you both grumble, but you still end up in front of the tree. As in Dickens's tale, the grump always comes round in the end.
duoNoel.p_scrooge_a: Make a deal: one tradition chosen by the one who loves Christmas, and one evening without a single string of lights for the other. Everybody wins.
duoNoel.q1: The Christmas decorations come out of their boxes:
duoNoel.q1c: Whenever we find a free weekend
duoNoel.q2a: Tall, color-coordinated, worthy of a shop window
duoNoel.q2b: Covered in handmade ornaments and keepsakes
duoNoel.q2c: A real one that smells of the forest, with three strings of lights
duoNoel.q2d: Small, or no tree at all: we're never home
duoNoel.q3a: A list for each person, all bought by early December
duoNoel.q3b: Handmade, or wrapped like works of art
duoNoel.q3c: One nice present that we give ourselves, together
duoNoel.q3d: At the last minute, if at all
duoNoel.q4a: At our place, and we're the ones hosting
duoNoel.q4b: On the road, between two families
duoNoel.q4c: Just the two of us, in pajamas
duoNoel.q5a: We cook for two days, and it's the best part
duoNoel.q5b: A beautiful table, candles, and we dress up
duoNoel.q5c: Everyone brings a dish, no fuss
duoNoel.q5d: Cheese fondue, a blanket and a movie
duoNoel.q6a: On repeat from November, we know all the words
duoNoel.q6c: In the car, to get through the miles
duoNoel.q6d: One sings, the other puts headphones on
duoNoel.q7a: The Christmas market, for the lights and the mulled wine
duoNoel.q7b: A long walk in the cold
duoNoel.q7d: Couch, hot chocolate and a Christmas movie
duoNoel.q8a: We gave one to the whole family
duoNoel.q8b: Only one of us wears one, the other rolls their eyes
duoNoel.q8c: A big warm sweater, Christmas or not
duoNoel.q9b: Dinner with one side, lunch with the other
duoNoel.q9c: A small group suits us fine
duoNoel.q9d: We love them, but two days, not three
duoNoel.q10a: Up first to see everyone's faces at the presents
duoNoel.q10b: A breakfast that lasts until noon
duoNoel.q10c: A lie-in, and presents under the covers
duoNoel.q11: What you like best about Christmas:
duoNoel.q11a: Making people happy, watching them open their presents
duoNoel.q11b: The lights, the shop windows, the stories
duoNoel.q12a: We head off again to see people
duoNoel.q12b: We get stuck into the puzzles, the games and the crafts
duoNoel.q12c: The mountains or the great outdoors, if we can
duoNoel.q12d: We don't see anyone, and it's lovely
